Rashi on Eruvin 42b:10:1.english: And since [regarding] walking - [Walking in] a pen and a fold on account of walking in an open field, we do not decree [a prohibition].

Rashi on Eruvin 42b:10:2.hebrew: טלטול אטו הילוך - כגון שבת בבקעה ביו"ט, שהילוך אסור לו חוץ לאלפים במקום שביתתו, וטלטול דזריקה מותר בלא מחיצות:
Rashi on Eruvin 42b:10:2.english: Carrying due to walking - For example, [in the case of one who] established residence in a valley on a Festival, where walking is forbidden to him beyond two thousand [cubits from] his place of residence, and carrying by [means of] throwing is permitted without partitions:

Rashi on Eruvin 42b:10:3.hebrew: לא גזרינן - שלא יטלטל בזריקה חוץ לאלפים אטו הילוך, שמא ימשך אחר חפצו, כרב נחמן. ואף על גב דבשבת בבקעה והקיפוהו נכרים לא סבירא להו כוותיה — דהא לדידהו, אע"ג דלא שבת באויר מחיצות, שרי — בהא מיהא כרב נחמן קיימי, דלא גזרי' שמא ימשך. אי נמי, בשבת בבקעה נמי סבירא להו כוותיה, דהא דשרו ליה הכא — משום דנאנס הוא:
Rashi on Eruvin 42b:10:3.english: We do not decree - That one may not carry by throwing beyond [his] two thousand [cubits] due to walking, lest he be drawn after his object, in accordance with [the view of] Rav Naḥman. And even though in [the case of one who] spent Shabbat in a valley and gentiles surrounded him [with a partition], they do not hold in accordance with him — for according to them, even though he did not spend Shabbat within the airspace of partitions, [walking the entire area] is permitted — in this [matter], at least, they stand in accordance with Rav Naḥman: that we do not decree lest he be drawn [after his object]. Alternatively, in [the case of one who] spent Shabbat in a valley, they also hold in accordance with him; and that which they permitted him here [in a pen or stable] is because he was coerced.

Rashi on Eruvin 42b:12:1.hebrew: שני מקומות הן - ולא דמי אהדדי: דיר וסהר יש להן מחיצות, בקעה אין לה מחיצה; הלכך לא מיחלפי:
Rashi on Eruvin 42b:12:1.english: They are two places - And they are not similar to each other: a pen and a fold have partitions, [whereas] an open field does not have a partition; therefore, they will not be confused.

Rashi on Eruvin 42b:13:1.hebrew: אבל טלטול אטו הילוך - כגון ששבת בבקעה ביו"ט, אימא דגזרי שלא יטלטל בזריקה חוץ לאלפים שמא ימשך אחר חפצו, דהא חד מקום הוא, ולית להו דרב נחמן כלל:
Rashi on Eruvin 42b:13:1.english: However, carrying due to walking - For example, where one established [his] Sabbath rest in a valley on Yom Tov, say that they decree that he may not move [an object] by throwing [it] beyond two thousand [cubits], lest he be drawn after his object, since it is a single place; and they do not accept Rav Nachman's [ruling] at all.

Rashi on Eruvin 42b:15:1.hebrew: אבל היכא דלא שבת - לא הוי כארבע אמות, ולהכי לא מישתרי בהילוך. אבל טלטול דזריקה — לעולם אימא לך דשרי ליה בכל הדיר וסהר בזריקה, ולא גזרינן שמא יזוז וימשך:
Rashi on Eruvin 42b:15:1.english: However, where he did not establish residence - It is not [considered] like four cubits, and therefore it is not permitted for walking. But moving [an object] by throwing — I could always tell you that it is permitted for him throughout the entire pen and stable by throwing, and we do not decree lest he move and be drawn [after it].

Rashi on Eruvin 42b:18:1.english: Since he acquired [Shabbat] residence - The boat is [considered] for him like four cubits.

Rashi on Eruvin 42b:19:1.hebrew: נוטלתו מתחילת ד' ומניחתו לסוף ארבע - כלומר, משיצא זה חוץ לתחום, לא נקט ליה ארבע אמות, דספינה כל שעה היא מהלכת, בכל קפיצה וקפיצה יותר מארבע אמות. נמצא שאין לה תורת ארבע אמות כלל, שלא עמד פסיעה אחת בתוך ארבע אמות; הלכך, לא קנו לו ארבע אמות. לישנא אחרינא: כגון שהספינה הולכת למזרח והוא מהלך בתוכה למערב, שהספינה מחזירתו כל שעה לתוך ארבע אמותיו. וקשיא לי: תינח הליכה, אבל אם חזר לראש האחר היכי מישתרי? ובמתני' לא חילק רבן גמליאל בין שהוא מהלך לצד זה בין שהוא מהלך לצד שהספינה מהלכת. וזהו לשון דודי ר' שמעון מפי הרב. ל"א: כלומר, כשעוקר את רגלו, קודם שיניחנה הספינה מוציאתו מד' אמות שלו ונכנס לתוך ארבע אמות אחרות על כרחו, והוה ליה כמי שהוציאוהו נכרי חוץ מארבע אמותיו ונתנוהו לתוך ארבע אמות אחרות שנותנין לו ד' אמות, וכן לעולם. וזה עיקר:
Rashi on Eruvin 42b:19:1.english: Lifts him from the beginning of four [cubits] and places him at the end of four - That is to say, from the moment this [person] went outside the Shabbat boundary [techum], four cubits were not established for him, because the boat is moving at every moment, [advancing] more than four cubits with each and every surge. It follows that it has no status of four cubits at all, for he did not stand [even] a single step within [a fixed] four cubits; therefore, four cubits were not acquired for him. Another version: For example, where the boat is traveling eastward and he is walking westward within it, such that the boat continuously brings him back into his [original] four cubits. And this is difficult to me: This works well for walking [westward], but if he turned back toward the other end, how would it be permitted? And in the Mishnah, Rabban Gamliel did not differentiate between whether he walks in this direction or whether he walks in the direction that the boat is traveling. And this was the wording of my uncle, Rabbi Shimon, from the mouth of the Rav. Another explanation: That is to say, when he lifts his foot, before he sets it down, the boat carries him out of his four cubits and he enters into another four cubits against his will; and he is [treated] like one whom a gentile removed outside his four cubits and placed into another four cubits, to whom [the Sages] grant four cubits, and so on indefinitely. And this is the primary [explanation].

Rashi on Eruvin 42b:1:1.hebrew: היה מודד ובא - הנותן עירובו ובא לילך ממקום עירובו אלפים, וכלתה מדתו בחצי עיר אחרת שעירבו את כולה, אי נמי ביו"ט:
Rashi on Eruvin 42b:1:1.english: He was measuring and coming - One who placed his [techum] eiruv and came to walk two thousand [cubits] from the place of his eiruv, and his measure ended in the middle of another city where they made an eiruv for all of it; or alternatively, on Yom Tov.

Rashi on Eruvin 42b:1:2.hebrew: שלא יעבור תחום - אלפים ממקום עירובו ברגליו, דכיון דלא שבת בתוכה, לא הויא ליה כד' אמות:
Rashi on Eruvin 42b:1:2.english: That he does not overstep the limit - [i.e., the] two thousand [cubits] from the place of his eiruv on foot; for since he did not spend Shabbat within it, it is not [considered] for him like four cubits.

Rashi on Eruvin 42b:1:3.hebrew: במאי מטלטל - בכל העיר, הואיל ותני שלא יעבור את התחום ברגליו:
Rashi on Eruvin 42b:1:3.english: How does he carry - [How can he carry] throughout the entire city, since [the baraita] teaches that he may not overstep the [Shabbat] limit with his feet?

Rashi on Eruvin 42b:1:4.english: Is it not by means of throwing - Evidently, we do not decree lest he be drawn [after it].

Rashi on Eruvin 42b:20:1.hebrew: מאי בינייהו - בין רבה לר' זירא:
Rashi on Eruvin 42b:20:1.english: What is [the practical difference] between them - Between Rabba and Rabbi Zeira.

Rashi on Eruvin 42b:20:2.hebrew: שנפחתו דופני הספינה - וביטלו המחיצות — דרבה ליתא, דר' זירא איתא:
Rashi on Eruvin 42b:20:2.english: Where the walls of the boat were breached - And the partitions were nullified — [the reason] of Rabba does not apply, [while the reason] of Rabbi Zeira applies.

Rashi on Eruvin 42b:20:3.hebrew: אי נמי בקופץ מספינה לספינה - ובאויר מחיצותיה של זו לא שבת. לרבה, אין יכול להלך בזו; ולרבי זירא, שרי:
Rashi on Eruvin 42b:20:3.english: Alternatively, in [the case of] one who jumps from boat to boat - And within the airspace of the partitions of this [second boat] he had not rested [at the onset of Shabbat]. According to Rabba, he cannot walk in this [boat]; and according to Rabbi Zeira, it is permitted.

Rashi on Eruvin 42b:2:1.hebrew: לא במשיכה - לא גרסי'. ומאן דגריס לה, הכי קאמר: ורב הונא אמר לך, האי דקתני "מותר לטלטל בכל העיר כולה" — במשיכה קאמר, שמושך מחוץ לאלפים לתוך אלפים; דהתם ליכא למיגזר שמא ימשך, דלאו חפציו הוא עד דמייתי ליה לגואי, וכי מייתי ליה — תו לא מפיק ליה:
Rashi on Eruvin 42b:2:1.english: No, by [way of] pulling - We do not read [this]. And one who does read it, this is what it means: Rav Huna [could] say to you, that which [the baraita] teaches, "[he is] permitted to carry throughout the entire city," means by [way of] pulling, in that he pulls [an object] from outside the two thousand [cubits] into the two thousand [cubits]; for there, there is no [reason] to decree lest he be drawn [after it], since it is not [considered] his object until he brings it inside, and once he brings it [inside], he will no longer take it out.

Rashi on Eruvin 42b:3:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן - אמר רב הונא: היה מודד ובא, וכלתה מדתו בחצי חצר — אין לו אלא חצי חצר להלך:
Rashi on Eruvin 42b:3:1.english: This is the text we read: - Rav Huna said: [If] one was measuring and coming, and his measurement ended in the middle of a courtyard, he has only half the courtyard to walk.

Rashi on Eruvin 42b:4:1.english: It is obvious - For his two thousand [cubits] have ended.

Rashi on Eruvin 42b:4:2.hebrew: אימא יש לו חצי חצר - אותו חצי של חצר שבתוך תחומו, מותר להלך כי אורחיה. והתירא איצטריכא לאשמועינן, ולאו איסורא דאידך פלגא:
Rashi on Eruvin 42b:4:2.english: Say: He has half a courtyard - [In] that half of the courtyard that is within his [Shabbat] limit, he is permitted to walk in his usual manner. And it was necessary to teach us the permission, and not the prohibition of the other half.

Rashi on Eruvin 42b:5:1.english: This too is obvious - That he has the half that is within his measure.

Rashi on Eruvin 42b:5:2.hebrew: <span class="parenthesized">(<abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr>: אמר רב הונא: היה מודד ובא, וכלתה מדתו בחצי חצר — אין לו אלא חצי חצר:
Rashi on Eruvin 42b:5:2.english: (This is the reading: Rav Huna said: [If] one was measuring and coming, and his measurement ended in the middle of a courtyard, he has only half the courtyard.

Rashi on Eruvin 42b:5:3.english: [It is] obvious - For behold, we have heard Rav Huna decree [a prohibition] lest [one] be drawn [after it].

Rashi on Eruvin 42b:5:4.hebrew: אימא יש לו חצי חצר - אותו חצי חצר שבתוך תחומו, מותר לטלטל כי אורחיה. והתירא איצטריך לאשמועי', ולאו איסורא דאידך פלגא:
Rashi on Eruvin 42b:5:4.english: Say: He has half a courtyard - In that half of the courtyard that is within his [Shabbat] limit, it is permitted to carry in the normal manner. And it was necessary to teach us the permission, and not the prohibition of the other half.

Rashi on Eruvin 42b:5:5.hebrew: הא נמי פשיטא - דפלגא דבתוך מדתו שרי, דלא דמי לשבת בבקעה, דהתם איכא למיסר לטלטולי אפי' בתוך אלפים משום טעמא דנפרצה, דההיא ודאי נפרצה לקמום האסור לה; שהרי מחיצות הללו לא היו כאן מבעוד יום, והיתה אסורה לכל אדם, וכשהוקפה בשבת והועילו לזה שבתוכו לאלפים — הועילו לו ולא לחוץ אלפים שהן חוץ מתחומו, והאי חוץ לאלפים לא היה לו שום היתר אצל שום אדם, הלכך הוי מקום האסור ואוסר. אבל חצר, אין לומר בה חילוק פירצה למקום האסור, דהא מבעוד יום חדא היא; ונהי דאסרי להאי לטלטולי חוץ לאלפים על ידי זריקה משום שמא ימשך — אבל בתוך מדת תחומו מותר לטלטולי כי אורחיה):
Rashi on Eruvin 42b:5:5.english: This too is obvious - That the half [of the courtyard] that is within his measure is permitted [for carrying], for it is not comparable to [one who] established Shabbat residence in a valley, where there is [reason] to prohibit carrying even within [his] two thousand [cubits] due to the rationale of [a partition that is] breached [to a place forbidden to it]. For that [area within the two thousand cubits] was indeed breached to a place that is forbidden to it, since these partitions were not here while it was yet day, and [the valley] was forbidden to all people; and when it was enclosed on Shabbat and [the partitions] were effective for this person within it for [his] two thousand [cubits], they were effective for him, but not for [the area] beyond the two thousand [cubits] that is beyond his Shabbat limit; and this [area] beyond the two thousand [cubits] never had any permissibility for any person; therefore, it is a forbidden place and renders [the permitted area] forbidden. However, regarding a courtyard, one cannot apply to it a distinction of a breach into a forbidden place, for while it was yet day it was a single [domain]; and although we prohibit this person from carrying beyond the two thousand [cubits] by means of throwing, lest he be drawn [after his object], nevertheless, within the measure of his Shabbat limit, it is permitted to carry in his usual manner.)

Rashi on Eruvin 42b:6:1.hebrew: מודה לי הונא - אע"ג דגזר שמא ימשך:
Rashi on Eruvin 42b:6:1.english: Huna agrees with me - Even though he decreed [elsewhere] lest one be drawn [after it].

Rashi on Eruvin 42b:6:2.hebrew: היה מודד ובא וכלתה מדתו על שפת תקרה - כנגד שפת הקירוי, והבית חוץ למדתו הוא. וכגון שנפרץ כותל הבית, שנשתייר מלמעלה קירוי, ונפרץ בית לחצר שבפניה, דלא הוי בית נפרץ למקום האסור:
Rashi on Eruvin 42b:6:2.english: He was measuring and his measurement ended at the edge of the ceiling - [That is,] opposite the edge of the roofing, and the house is outside his measurement. And [this is in a case] such as where the wall of the house was breached, [such] that roofing remained above, and the house was breached into the courtyard in front of it, so that the house is not breached into a forbidden place.

Rashi on Eruvin 42b:6:3.hebrew: מותר לטלטל בכל הבית - ע"י זריקה, ואע"פ שאסור ליכנס לתוכה ברגליו. והכא לא גזרינן שמא ימשך, הואיל ותקרות הבית חובטות — כלומר נראות כיורדות וסותמות — ואיכא היכר ולא ממשיך; שהרי עיניו נותן בתקרה, וסימן הוא ששם כלתה מדתו:
Rashi on Eruvin 42b:6:3.english: [He is] permitted to carry throughout the entire house - By means of throwing, even though it is forbidden to enter into it on foot. And here, we do not decree lest he be drawn [after the object], since the ceilings of the house press down — that is to say, they are seen as descending and closing off [the space] — and there is a recognizable distinction, and he will not be drawn [after it]; for he sets his eyes upon the ceiling, and it is a sign that there his measurement ended.

Rashi on Eruvin 42b:8:1.hebrew: כתנאי - אי גזרינן שמא ימשך, אי לא:
Rashi on Eruvin 42b:8:1.english: [It is parallel to a dispute between] Tannaim - Whether we decree lest he be drawn [after his object] or not.

Rashi on Eruvin 42b:9:1.english: That we do not decree [prohibiting] walking in a pen or a corral - In a case where gentiles placed him in it.

Rashi on Eruvin 42b:9:2.hebrew: אטו הילוך דבקעה - דאין בה מחיצות, דהתם אין לו אלא ד' אמות, כדתנן בריש פירקין. ובדיר וסהר, אע"ג דלא שבת באויר מחיצותיהן מבעוד יום, כארבע אמות דמיין ליה, הואיל ובאונס יצא מתחומו:
Rashi on Eruvin 42b:9:2.english: Is [walking in an open field comparable] - Which has no partitions, for there he has only four cubits, as we learned at the beginning of our chapter. And in a pen or a corral, even though he did not establish his Shabbat residence within the airspace of their partitions while it was still day, they are considered like four cubits for him, since he left his boundary under duress.

Tosafot on Eruvin 42b:15:1.hebrew: אבל היכא דלא שבת באויר מחיצות מבעוד יום - וא"ת: והרי ספינה, דשבת באויר מחיצות מבעוד יום, ומוכיח לקמן דפליגי? וי"ל: דקסבר מחיצות להבריח מים עשויות:
Tosafot on Eruvin 42b:15:1.english: "However, where he did not acquire his place of residence within the airspace of partitions while it was still day" - And if you say: But what about a boat, where he acquired his place of residence within the airspace of partitions while it was still day, and [the Gemara] proves below that they dispute [this as well]? One can say: He holds that partitions [of a boat] are made [only] to keep water out.

Tosafot on Eruvin 42b:21:1.hebrew: ורבי זירא מ"ט לא אמר כרבה - פירוש: ויתיר אפי' בהעמדה. וא"ת: מאי קבעי? מההוא טעמא דלית להו לר' יהושע ור' עקיבא — מאותן סברות לית להו לדידהו דהדדי! וי"ל: דלר' יהושע ור' עקיבא ניחא, דאית להו בכל מקום שהוא חוץ לתחום דאין לו אלא ד' אמות, ולא מפלגי בין דיר וסהר וספינה. אבל רבה ורבי זירא, דמפלגי בין דיר וסהר וספינה, בעי שפיר: מר אמאי לא אמר כמר, שמטעם זה יש לחלק ביניהם:
Tosafot on Eruvin 42b:21:1.english: "And Rabbi Zeira, what is the reason he did not say in accordance with Rabba?" - Explanation: And [thereby] permit [walking through the entire boat] even when it is stationary. And if you say: What is [the Gemara] asking? For the [very] reason that Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Akiva do not accept [Rabban Gamliel's position] — based on those [same] rationales they [Rabba and Rabbi Zeira] do not accept each other's [views]! And one can say: As for Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Akiva, it is understandable, for they hold that wherever one is outside the [Shabbat] limit, he has only four cubits, and they do not distinguish between a pen, a stable, and a boat. But Rabba and Rabbi Zeira, who distinguish between a pen and a stable, and a boat, [the Gemara] rightly asks: Why did one Master not say like the other Master, since for this reason [too] one can distinguish between them.

Tosafot on Eruvin 42b:2:1.hebrew: לא ע"י משיכה - כי שקיל מבראי לגואי, ליכא למיחש שמא ימשך אחר חפצו; אלא כשזורק מגואי לבראי, דמרחיק החפץ ממנו. והא דאמר רב הונא "אין מטלטלין אלא בארבע", היינו כלפי צד אבראי — לטלטל כי אורחיה או לזרוק, דלענין זה נפרצה במלואה למקום האסור לה; אבל במשיכה, מטלטל בכל מקום, דלענין זה לא נפרצה במלואה למקום האסור לה. וכענין זה יש בכל גגות (לקמן עירובין דף פט.), דאסר רב לטלטל טפי מארבע בכלים דבית לגג, אע"ג דכלים דגג שרי לטלטל בכל הגגין כרבי שמעון, והוי למקום המותר לו:
Tosafot on Eruvin 42b:2:1.english: "No, by means of pulling" - When one takes [an object] from the outside to the inside, there is no concern lest he be drawn after his object; rather, [this concern applies only] when one throws from the inside to the outside, as he moves the object away from himself. And that which Rav Huna said, "One may carry only within four [cubits]" — that is towards the outer side, [whether] to carry in his usual manner or to throw, for regarding this, [the permitted area] is breached in its entirety to a place that is forbidden to it; but by means of pulling, one may carry anywhere, for regarding this, it is not breached in its entirety to a place that is forbidden to it. And there is a similar case in [the chapter] "Kol Gagot" (below, Eruvin 89a), where Rav prohibited carrying utensils of a house more than four [cubits] to a roof, even though utensils of a roof are permitted to be carried throughout all the roofs in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, and it is [being moved] to a place that is permitted to it.

Tosafot on Eruvin 42b:3:1.hebrew: [אמר רב הונא היה מודד ובא - ותימה לי: לרב הונא, היכי מטלטל בחצי חצר? הא נפרץ למקום האסור לו! ורש"י פי': להלך. וקשה: ל' "לטלטולי" לא משמע להלך! ועוד, הא אשמעינן לעיל בבקעה דמהלך אלפים, ולא גזרי' דילמא אתי להלוכי חוץ לאלפים! וי"ל: לענין טלטול, יש לחלק בין בקעה לחצר — כיון דלגבי אחריני חשיב מחיצה בחצר, לא חשיב נפרץ למקום האסור לה. ואי להלך, כפי' רש"י — איצטריך רב הונא לאשמעינן: אע"ג דשייך טפי למיגזר בחצר מבבקעה, אפ"ה לא גזרינן. תוספות שאנ"ץ]:
Tosafot on Eruvin 42b:3:1.english: ["Rav Huna said: If a person was measuring and came" - And it is astonishing to me: according to Rav Huna, how may he carry in half the courtyard? Behold, it is breached into a place that is forbidden to him! And Rashi explained: [it means] to walk. And this is difficult: the expression "to carry" does not imply "to walk"! And furthermore, [the Gemara] already taught us earlier regarding a valley that one may walk two thousand [cubits], and we do not decree lest he come to walk beyond the two thousand [cubits]! And one can say: regarding carrying, one can differentiate between a valley and a courtyard — since with respect to others it is considered a partition in a courtyard, it is not considered breached into a place that is forbidden to it. And if [it means] to walk, according to Rashi's explanation — Rav Huna needed to teach us [this, because] even though it is more applicable to decree in a courtyard than in a valley, even so we do not decree. [Tosafot of Sens]:

Tosafot on Eruvin 42b:3:2.hebrew: וכלתה מדתו בחצי חצר - גרסינן, דחצי העיר שמעינן ליה ממתני' דכיצד מעברין (לקמן עירובין דף סא.). וא"ת: חצר נמי פשיטא, דמאי שנא ממערה, דתנן בכיצד מעברין (שם): "ולמודד שאמרו נותנין לו אלפים אמה, שאפי' כלתה מדתו במערה" — דמשמע דיש לו חצי מערה? ואין לומר דהתם מיירי בכלתה מדתו בסוף המערה — מדקאמר בגמרא (שם): "סוף העיר אצטריכא ליה, דלא תנן"! וי"ל, דמערה לא שכיחא בה כלים, ושייך למיגזר טפי בחצר מבמערה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 42b:3:2.english: "And his measuring ended in the middle of a courtyard" - We read [in our text: "in the middle of a courtyard"], as [the law regarding] half the city we learn from the Mishnah in Keitzad Me’abrin (below, Eruvin 61a). And if you say: A courtyard should also be obvious, for how is it different from a cave, as we learned in the Mishnah in Keitzad Me’abrin (there): "And concerning the surveyor about whom they said: They give him two thousand cubits, that even if his measurement ended in a cave" — which implies that he has [only] half the cave? And one cannot say that there it is dealing with [a case where] his measurement ended at the [far] end of the cave — since [the Gemara] says in the Gemara (there): "[The case of] the end of the city was necessary for him [to state], as we did not learn [it in the Mishnah]"! And one can say: In a cave utensils are not commonly found, and it is more applicable to issue a decree in a courtyard than in a cave.

Tosafot on Eruvin 42b:8:1.hebrew: כתנאי (או) הוליכוהו לעיר אחרת - קצת קשה, דהשתא בעי לאוקומי שמואל כר"ג, ושמואל לא פסיק לקמן כר"ג אלא בספינה. וי"ל, דהוה מצי למימר: וליטעמיך:
Tosafot on Eruvin 42b:8:1.english: "[Parallel to] tanna’im" (or) "They brought him to another city" - It is somewhat difficult, for now [the Gemara] seeks to establish [the opinion of] Shmuel in accordance with Rabban Gamliel, yet Shmuel does not rule below in accordance with Rabban Gamliel except in [the case of] a ship. And it can be said that [the Gemara] could have said: "And according to your reasoning..."
